extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in construction/AEC interested in digital technologies and systematic review methods
extracted.subtask_description: A PRISMA-2020–based systematic review synthesizing evidence on adoption and implementation of emerging digital technologies in the construction industry, mapping applications, barriers, trends, and future research directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to PRISMA 2020 framework
rubrics_metrics.description: The study follows the PRISMA 2020 framework to ensure methodological transparency, reproducibility, and comprehensiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PRISMA 2020 reporting items throughout the review (search strategy, selection process, data extraction, synthesis, reporting of results and limitations) to make methods and findings transparent and reproducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive database search
rubrics_metrics.description: A comprehensive search was conducted across multiple academic databases, including Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, IEEE Xplore, Taylor & Francis Online, and ASCE Library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search multiple major bibliographic databases to capture literature across engineering, computer science, and construction domains; document database names, search strings, and dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defined publication timeframe
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrict searches to the specified publication window and justify timeframe choice; report start and end dates used in searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include peer-reviewed studies
rubrics_metrics.description: After applying inclusion and exclusion criteria, 105 peer-reviewed studies were included for qualitative synthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit inclusion to peer-reviewed literature (unless otherwise justified), and report the number of included studies and reasons for excluding non–peer-reviewed sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply transparent inclusion and exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies were screened using inclusion and exclusion criteria to select eligible papers for synthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify eligibility criteria (population/domain, interventions/technologies, outcomes, study types, languages), describe screening workflow (e.g., number of reviewers, conflict resolution), and report reasons for exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use qualitative synthesis for heterogeneous evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: 105 peer-reviewed studies were included for qualitative synthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When studies are diverse in methods and outcomes, synthesize findings thematically or narratively, and explain synthesis approach and coding frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map key applications across construction project phases
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine the key applications of emerging technologies across different construction project phases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify and report technology applications by lifecycle phase (e.g., design, construction, operation), providing examples and counts where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify technical, managerial, financial, and contextual challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine the technical, managerial, financial, and contextual challenges affecting adoption of emerging technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract and categorize barriers/enablers reported in studies (technical interoperability, cost, managerial readiness, regulatory/contextual factors) and discuss their prevalence and implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze geographical and methodological trends
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine the geographical and methodological trends in the literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report regional distribution of studies, study designs and methods used, and how methodological choices vary by geography or technology domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover specified technology domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on technologies such as Big Data, Artificial Intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), Cloud Computing, the Metaverse, and Information Retrieval (IR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define included technology categories up front, map each included study to one or more technologies, and discuss cross-technology integration where reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify research gaps and future research directions
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify research gaps, particularly concerning interoperability, workforce readiness, and data governance, and propose future research directions for integrated and sustainable digital transformation in construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synthesize gaps found across studies, prioritize or cluster gaps (e.g., technical, socio-organizational, policy), and provide specific, actionable future research questions or agendas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a conceptual framework to guide research and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Development of a conceptual framework guiding future cross-technology research and practical adoption strategies in the AEC sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on synthesized evidence, propose a conceptual model that links technologies, applications, barriers/enablers, and outcomes to guide further empirical work and practitioner adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce a consolidated evidence base mapping applications, barriers, and enablers across lifecycle
rubrics_metrics.description: A consolidated evidence base mapping applications, barriers, and enablers of emerging technologies across the construction lifecycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present synthesized mappings (tables, figures, thematic maps) that clearly show relationships between technologies, lifecycle phases, and reported barriers/enablers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure methodological transparency, reproducibility, and comprehensiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The review aims to ensure methodological transparency, reproducibility, and comprehensiveness (stated as an overall objective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full search strategies, data extraction templates, study coding schemes, and, where possible, share data/code (e.g., via OSF) to allow replication and reuse.
